title: Illinois's 10th Congressional District general election, 2026
description: The general election for Illinois's 10th congressional district pits incumbent Democrat Brad Schneider against Republican challenger Carl Lambrecht. The district covers Chicago's affluent North Shore suburbs including Highland Park, Deerfield, and Waukegan. Once a perennial swing seat, the district has shifted leftward and is rated Solidly Democratic by the Cook Political Report (D+12 PVI). Schneider, a six-term congressman and chair of the New Democrat Coalition, defeated primary challenger Morgan Coghill with 78.8% of the vote in March, while Lambrecht won the Republican primary uncontested. The race centers on federal economic policy, healthcare, and abortion rights, with Schneider emphasizing his moderate record and ability to deliver for the district.
polling_note: No publicly available opinion polls were found for the 2026 general election matchup in Illinois's 10th congressional district. The race is rated 'Solid D' by Cook Political Report.

candidates.name: Brad Schneider
candidates.summary: Brad Schneider is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Illinois's 10th congressional district, first elected in 2012. He chairs the New Democrat Coalition, the largest ideological caucus in the House Democratic Caucus, and has focused on healthcare access, gun violence prevention, and pro-Israel policy. Schneider previously served one term from 2013-2015 before losing reelection, then won back the seat in 2016 and has been reelected comfortably since.

candidates.summary: Carl Lambrecht is the Republican nominee for U.S. House in Illinois's 10th congressional district. He ran uncontested in the March 2026 Republican primary and previously ran as the Republican candidate for Illinois House District 58 in 2024. Lambrecht is a resident of Highland Park and has campaigned on conservative economic and fiscal positions.

forecast.rationale: No public general-election polling is available for this race, so confidence is capped at medium and the forecast is driven entirely by district fundamentals. Illinois's 10th district carries a Cook PVI of D+12 and is rated Solidly Democratic by the Cook Political Report, reflecting a strong Democratic lean following leftward shifts in this historically swingy North Shore district. Incumbent Brad Schneider is a six-term Democratic congressman and chair of the New Democrat Coalition who won his primary with 78.8% of the vote. Republican challenger Carl Lambrecht was uncontested in his primary and has no elected office experience, having previously run unsuccessfully for the Illinois House. Without any contrary polling evidence, the combination of a D+12 partisan baseline, entrenched six-term incumbency, and a relatively unknown challenger supports a safe Democratic outcome.
